Peng et al. identify the tolerogenic maternal microchimeric subset (LysM+ CD11c+ Vav1+), a conditional depletion handle (maternal-only DTR + diphtheria toxin), two functional readouts of noninherited-maternal-antigen (NIMA) tolerance (NIMA-specific FOXP3+ Treg expansion; cross-generational resiliency against fetal wastage), and the fact that the tolerance requires ongoing stimulation while the cells persist autonomously. These let the comparison be stated as a matched pair: tolerance sustained by the offspring's own persisting maternal cells, against tolerance sustained by matched tolerogenic cells given later from a donor.
